Protein digestion and bioavailability
377


of proteins in the stomach involves the actions of pepsins, which are secreted as the precursor pepsinogen by the gastric mucosa
main cells. The release of pepsinogens is induced by gastrin, histamine, and cholinergic stimulation and pepsinogens are converted
to the active form pepsins by the loss of a small basic peptide. Pepsins are most active at a pH of approximately 2 and totally inactive
at a pH above approximately 5. So, for pepsins to produce any digestive action on protein, the stomach juices must be acidic.
